Advisory.Description:
## Root Cause
The Toolbox settings-tree helpers recurse over the parsed element tree without any depth
bound. `_to_settings_string` (`nltk/toolbox.py:418`), `remove_blanks`
(`nltk/toolbox.py:432`), `add_default_fields` (`nltk/toolbox.py:451`), `_sort_fields`
(`nltk/toolbox.py:484`), and `add_blank_lines` (`nltk/toolbox.py:502,516`) each recurse once
per element level with no depth counter or explicit stack. The producer
`ToolboxSettings.parse` builds the element tree iteratively, so nesting depth is driven
entirely by attacker-supplied `\+marker` / `\-marker` pairs.

## Impact
An application that parses an untrusted Toolbox settings file and then serialises or
transforms it through any of the public helper functions aborts with an unhandled
`RecursionError`, terminating the affected operation or request worker (denial of service,
CWE-674). The recursion is pure Python, yielding a catchable `RecursionError` rather than
memory corruption or code execution. Confidentiality and integrity are unaffected.

## Attack Chain
1. The application parses an untrusted settings file via `ToolboxSettings.open_string` /
   `open` plus `parse`, producing an *N*-deep element tree; parsing is iterative and
   completes without error.
2. The application passes the tree to a public helper — `to_settings_string`,
   `remove_blanks`, `add_default_fields`, `sort_fields`, or `add_blank_lines` — as in the
   module's own parse-then-serialise round trip.
3. The helper recurses once per element level with no depth guard, consuming call-stack
   frames. This holds even when the helper's configuration dictionaries are empty.
4. Once the nesting depth exceeds the interpreter recursion limit, an unhandled
   `RecursionError` propagates out of the public API.

## Bypass Evidence
Against the shipped source at the default recursion limit, a settings input nested 5 levels
deep traverses cleanly through every helper, while a well-formed input nested 5000 levels
deep drives each of the five helpers to an unhandled `RecursionError`; the iterative parse
builds the 4999-deep tree without error, isolating the fault to the recursive helpers. The
config-taking helpers (`add_default_fields`, `sort_fields`, `add_blank_lines`) recurse to
failure even with empty configuration dictionaries. A repository-wide search confirms no
depth guard exists anywhere in this module.

## Suggested Fix
Cap nesting depth at the shared producer `ToolboxSettings.parse` (the choke point that
builds the tree), or convert the five helpers to iterative traversals / add a shared
recursion-depth bound, so all consumers are protected by one fix.

Reported by pi (GitHub: @manus-pi).

## Fix status (2026-09-28)

Status: MERGED on develop (unreleased; v3.10.3 of 2026-08-12 predates the fix).

PR: #3885 "Bound recursion depth in parsers and traversal helpers" (ekaf), merged 2026-09-11, merge commit e521ecafc on develop.

Fix commit: 0b6975377 (nltk/toolbox.py: the settings helpers stop at MAX_TOOLBOX_DEPTH=500 with ValueError).

Probe: nltk/test/unit/security_probes/ghsa_f2h2_f4fc_p978.py (added in 2a6704952 on that PR); verdict on develop 2fa3f48fe: FIXED (bounded during parse (ValueError)).

Release: none yet; no release tag contains e521ecafc.
